errors.what: PHASE_SCHED hard-coded for four processes and filtered only inside build_stream; at NP=2 the final 'fade' phase was the least non-stationary, process 0 never faded, the phase banner printed non-existent processes, was_active was wrong for every NP<4, and UNLEARN marked EVERY process as faded (so the unlearn-a-faded-process test reported passing without ever running)
seg_from always seeks a random offset, so even a single-corpus stream teleports every 8-20 kB; more than half of English's assembled domains were our own seek artefacts (31 vs 13)
IndexError: `_wn = _oid[_w.argmax(-1)]` treated a global node id as a rank (index 4 out of bounds for size 2)

SIG_WIN=0 meant 'use WIN' i.e. 256 BYTES while the loop advances WIN TOKENS -- the signature encoder was reading 42% of the stream once the vocabulary compressed. Every domain result the project ever produced was measured through a partially-blind encoder

Claude's own fix for the above recomputed _sigw live, so asm.wins held windows of two widths and rekey died: 'ValueError: expected sequence of length 384 at dim 1 (got 426)'. Killed BOTH arms of the researcher's first real pilot. Worse than a crash: a moving width makes centroids incomparable
The smoke gate certified the change that killed the pilot -- every arm ran 12 kB, where the vocabulary barely grows, so no arm exercised tokenizer growth + rekey
Smoke gate took 4967s vs 479s; feared a regression from the signature widening

MAX_DOMAINS defaults to 64 with the comment 'mirroring the expert bank's fixed slot pool', but every launcher set MAX_DOMAINS=1000000 while leaving FAB_NMAX=64 -- the two populations designed as duals ran 15,625x apart

Domains were merged but essentially never culled (0 culls in the first 1000 pilot steps against 5-8 merges per manage), because the cull rule needed `act < min_size AND unseen > stale`, a conjunction an empty domain can fail forever

A stale `torch.stack(list(fab.keys))` left by the tensor refactor raised inside a try/except, silently deleting the ENTIRE EXPERTS and SUFFICIENCY output from the report with no sign it had been attempted

prompt.py -- the tool used to read generations, i.e. the deliverable -- carried a duplicated copy of Fabric and had been completely dead since the refactor (load_state_dict failed with ~300 missing keys). Nothing in the pipeline ever loaded a checkpoint back, so it went unnoticed for several commits
The `no_experts` smoke arm was vacuous -- EXPERTS is mutually exclusive with FABRIC, which wins the elif chain -- so it passed in every gate run while testing nothing

Optimizer moments were discarded on every resume: fab.grow() returns [] since the population became preallocated tensors, but the caller still called om.add_param_group on it, appending an EMPTY param group per growth event (60 growths -> 60 phantom groups -> load_state_dict count mismatch)

There was NO expert culling at all. router.manage() (create/replicate/cull) is gated on EXPERTS, mutually exclusive with FABRIC, so it never ran; the fabric population was grow-only. This is also why COMPETENCE PROTECTION reported 'spared 0' on every run
The [config] banner printed 'experts off' for a run with thousands of routed fabric experts -- EXPERTS names the legacy ExpertBank, not the live population
Every newborn expert was born as a blank identity (B=0): computes nothing -> no competence -> no routing mass -> no traffic -> can never acquire competence. A trap with no exit
Mutation jitter was an absolute 0.02 against weights of unknown scale, so a 'clone' was effectively an exact copy and the population explored nothing

Only the argmax winner's centroid ever moved (`s.cent[w.mean(0).argmax()]`), so the winner drifted toward everything it won while every other centroid stayed frozen at init -- expert discovery was impossible by construction

Routing was at BATCH granularity: `idx = w.mean(0).topk(kk)` and `_wk = _w[:, _oid[_ki]].mean(0)` gave all BATCH_W windows the same expert set and weights, making per-window specialization impossible. This made discovery/crossover/exploration incapable of helping

The per-window routing change broke prompt.py again -- it imported the classes but still duplicated the ENSEMBLE LOGIC (`_wk = _w[:, _oid]`). Gate failed 11/12 on the readback arm (RuntimeError: size of tensor a (4096) must match tensor b (2))

The chaining path computed EVERY expert at EVERY hop (Bo = (B,N,L,d)) -> CUDA OOM trying to allocate 11.39 GiB at 972 experts. Claude had written the comment warning about this and then recommended the flag anyway, costing the researcher a GPU run
With the OOM fixed, mean routed depth was 0.00 of 4 -- FAB_MIN_STEPS defaulted to 0 so HALT absorbed on the first hop. Chaining was switched on and nothing chained

The chaining transition matrix was memoryless: Q was one shared query, so R did not depend on which expert held the mass -- 'expert A hands to expert B' could not be learned. Caused by Claude collapsing the per-expert qproj during the scale refactor

Expert-identity representation collapse: every expert embedded to the SAME identity vector (typical nearest-neighbour distance 0.000). Explains routing landing arbitrarily on one node, SPECIALIZATION exactly 0.000, and the spawn never firing. The embedder had no VICReg/anti-collapse protection
The autoencoder/embedder loss ran only every FAB_EMB_EVERY=50 steps at weight 0.05 -- twelve weak updates in a short run, far too little to separate identities

FAB_SPAWN_DIST=0.45 was an absolute threshold on distance to the nearest of N identities, which shrinks as N grows -- spawning became impossible exactly when the population was large. SPAWNED BY SPECIFICATION: 0
Instrumentation bug: the identity nearest-neighbour distance meant to diagnose the collapse is only recorded inside spawn_from, which never runs when the bar is not met -- so it prints a stale 0.000

Claude ran two full 12-arm gates concurrently, competing for the same cores (gate took 4731s vs the usual 400-650s), and held the rm-predict push for ~an hour so the branch the researcher asked for did not exist on GitHub
Duplicated banner text -- '| competence protection ON | competence protection ON |' from a botched edit
